title: Prove sharp-order Clifford row-sum convergence (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove strict dimension monotonicity and sharp-order convergence for the full-projective-Clifford absolute Gram row sum at tensor width 4n+4. Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration.

```diff
- PR #5714: R_(2n) converges to T = sum_(k>=1) 2^(-k(k+1)/2)
+ R_(2n+2) > R_(2n)
+ 1/(2*4^n) <= T-R_(2n) <= (4+T)/(3*4^n), for every n>=1
```

The new step counts embeddings of each fixed alternating symmetrization, yielding a dimension-monotone residual-form average. It establishes the exact order Theta(4^(-n)); the envelope constants are not claimed optimal. The first verified refinement ended the research.

Credit Javier Vera / GosuBoy #5714 for the limiting row sum, Hiroki KUMAZAKI / kumagi #5694 for the nonsingular residual-form count, and Ali Romman #5526 for the residual correspondence and trace-lift framework. Their results are cited, not audited. The separate finite check uses the classical Rudvalis-Shinoda fixed-space distribution recorded by Fulman and Stanton, Theorem 2.3. The proof and verifier were produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

- Before: an asymptotic absolute-row-sum limit without this finite-dimension rate or monotonicity statement.
- After: a written all-dimension proof and exact corroboration over 22,914 ordered embeddings, 78 alternating Gram types, 20,336 invertible forms, 128 residual averages, 32 row sums and their 31 strict increases. Fifteen declared controls pass. Three separate implementation mutants reject at the intended embedding-product or gap diagnostic.
- CPython 3.12.15 on macOS 27.0.1 arm64: direct warning-strict normal and optimized runs pass in 0.25s and 0.26s. Both registered checks pass; each has a 120-second bound.
- Committed-byte and full source-history preflight pass at `f078a2c0630388feaac91c85254ab9f604df3b83`. Official export integrity/input coverage and both Git-free replays pass with exported files marked read-only and unchanged afterward. Receipts are generated from the five package source hashes.

From the repository root, exact local reproduction commands are:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/clifford-row-convergence/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/clifford-row-convergence/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-row-convergence
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-row-convergence --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_CLIFFORD_ROW_CONVERGENCE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Any standard-library CPython 3.12 installation can replace the local interpreter path. No runtime predecessor imports or external inputs are required. Base main is `19fdb086ea96af9a9f87936a2b888e10af4ed810`, priority revision 8, unchanged on the submission refresh.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem concerns the phase-insensitive absolute Gram row sum. It does not determine optimal Gram eigenvalues, the sharp leading error coefficient, a physical caller, a paid invoice or a new kappa. The selected-baseline binding check passed; full supplier, native, Lean, precision/tape and outer replays were not run because this isolated algebraic result does not claim those interfaces. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The five selected framework assumptions remain.

The original coverage-law card is explicitly changed to a conditioning side result in TASK.json. Overlap checks include live PR/Discussion data, main-tree and merged-PR searches and local reservations. Sparse local notes, unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs remain outside full coverage. No predecessor or selected-frontier file is modified.

## Open next questions

Evaluate the exact leading coefficient of 4^n(T-R_(2n)). Start with the residual-form average, prove a summable first-order expansion, and evaluate the symmetrization-rank distribution of nonsingular binary forms. This is not attempted or reserved here.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this finite-dimension Clifford absolute-row-sum quantity was found. The closeout refresh examined all thirteen other account PRs still open and created since the advance CLAIM. None computes this row sum or convergence envelope; no extra mathematical computations were run for comparison.

- #5943 concerns integer packing of equal-energy rows, including Clifford fixtures. Its packing radix and row-energy condition are different from the full-alphabet Gram absolute row sum here; no common numerical quantity is compared.
- #5940 concerns conditioned matching-layer norm interpolation. Its Gram inequality does not count projective Clifford displacement ranks or compute this row sum.

Merged #5714 and #5694 are the direct predecessors. Merged #5883 studies an odd-axis phase-sensitive spectral bound; this contribution does not extend it or claim a sharper spectral constant.
